title: A child's first dental visit
what: A pediatric dentist helps your child get to know the room and checks their teeth. Usually nothing is treated. The main goal is that your child is not scared.
why: It is usually advised to come when the first tooth comes in, and no later than age 1; after that, every 6 months for prevention.
tell_doctor: How your child brushes and who helps
If your child drinks milk, formula, or juice at night
If your child is afraid of doctors or something hurts

prepare.title: Mindset
prepare.text: Calmly tell your child the dentist will count their teeth. Do not scare them, and do not promise it will not hurt.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: Choose a time when your child is well rested and not hungry.

prepare.title: You
prepare.text: Your child senses your mood. Stay calm.

bring: Your child's toothbrush, if you want brushing checked
steps: The dentist meets your child and shows the tools
A young child is examined on your lap
The dentist counts the teeth and checks the gums
You are shown how to brush the teeth correctly
The dentist advises on toothpaste and eating habits
feel: It does not hurt your child
Your child may cry. That is normal and does not stop the exam
after: Praise your child for the visit
Brush your child's teeth twice a day
Come for checkups every 6 months, or as the dentist says

faq.q: Why treat baby teeth if they fall out?
faq.a: Decayed baby teeth hurt and can harm the adult teeth growing underneath.
That is normal. The dentist is experienced and knows how to help. The main thing is to stay calm yourself.

reminders.text: First dental visit soon. Your child should be rested and fed. Bring a favorite toy.
